import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/test_1.csv",

        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
        df = df.astype({
            'admit': 'int64',
            'gre': 'int64',
            'gpa': 'float64',
            'prestige': 'int64'
        })
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Since all sources have the same schema and no transformation is needed,
    # the combined dataframe matches the target schema.

    # Optional: Validate schema explicitly (not strictly necessary)
    expected_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
    combined_df = combined_df[expected_columns]

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_99/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
